paragraphs: Five timer reload words, indexed by the Speed Booster counter times two.
The first word also initializes the adjacent timer/counter pair: its low
byte is the initial delay and its high byte is the starting counter.
Later reloads are ORed into the low timer byte while preserving the counter.
Initial jump velocities for air, water, and lava/acid, in that order.
The integer and fractional components live in parallel speed/subspeed
tables. !SPF scales the velocity for the selected regional frame rate.
Each movement type selects a 12-byte row: acceleration, maximum speed,
then deceleration. Each value occupies two words; wordSwap places the
integer word before the fractional word consumed by the movement code.
SetTimer takes packed BCD minutes and seconds ($MMSS), not binary seconds.
Clear the old countdown before loading the duration and startup state.
SetTimer takes packed BCD minutes and seconds ($MMSS), not binary seconds.
Startup begins with an initial delay before the timer display moves into place.
Fuse countdown loaded for newly fired bombs before their explosion sequence.
regional selects the NTSC or PAL reload value.
Item messages wait for lag frames before accepting input. The collecting
PLM schedules the music-resume delay separately from this message wait.
The regular Zoomer shares its movement state machine with other crawlers.
InitAI_Zoomer_MZoomer chooses its starting orientation; MainAI_Crawlers
dispatches the handler installed by the orientation's animation script.
X is the enemy slot and Y points to the script's next word: a bank $A3
movement-handler address. Consume that word and return Y to the interpreter.
Zoomer/Zeela orientation lists install the handler before their first frame.
Their frame loops skip this command, so they do not overwrite a falling
handler on every animation cycle.
Before initialisation, Enemy.instList holds the population's initialisation
value, not a script pointer. Its low two bits select upside right, left,
down or up (0..3). Replace that value with the matching instruction list,
then fall through to the shared initialiser with X still the enemy slot.
Start with no visible spritemap and a do-nothing handler. An instruction
timer of one lets the orientation script install both on its next update.
Enemy.init0 selects the speed-table word copied into both velocity fields;
$00FF skips the lookup; existing velocities still pass through sign selection.
Crawling velocities are signed 8.8 pixels per frame, unlike the separate
integer/fractional word pair used while falling.
The low two property bits choose the initial velocity signs independently
of the script-orientation value: 0 negates X, 2 negates Y, 1 and 3 leave
both unchanged. These signs are also applied when the speed lookup was skipped.
These four orientation tables use Enemy.init1 directly as a byte offset
(0, 2, 4, 6, 8 or $0A), not an element number. It selects the species' script.
A corner turn chooses a new orientation list and resets the instruction timer
to one; that list installs the corresponding horizontal or vertical handler.
Crawler.function is a bank-local handler address, not a numeric state ID.
Tail-jump with X = EnemyIndex; the selected handler returns with RTL to
the AI caller. Orientation scripts and falling transitions share this field.
On a wall, X velocity presses into the surface and Y velocity moves along it.
A type $0014 earthquake at timer $001E saves this handler and selects falling.
That change does not return early: this invocation still performs its crawl step.
Convert signed 8.8 velocity to the movement helpers' signed 16.16 distance:
clear $12/$14, sign-extend, then store the velocity across $13/$14.
Add one pixel in the X direction to probe wall contact before travelling
along Y. The helpers return carry set on collision; $14.$12 is scratch
for the current move, not a persistent X- or Y-specific variable.
The wall probe collided, but travel along Y hit an inside corner.
Reverse X velocity and choose a floor/ceiling animation from the Y sign.
Restarting that script switches movement to the horizontal handler.
No wall contact: count this unsupported turn. Four consecutive misses
save the current handler and select falling instead of turning again.
Earlier misses reverse Y and select a floor/ceiling script to follow
the outside corner. Finding wall contact resets the shared turn counter.
Falling uses a separate signed 16.16 Y velocity: $14 receives the integer
word and $12 the fractional word. Move first, then accelerate if unobstructed.
A collision restores nonFallingFunction after clearing fall speed and the
turn counter. For the $00FF speed-lookup sentinel, landing first assigns
$0080 (0.5 pixels per frame) to both crawling velocities.
Add $8000 to the fractional word in NTSC, or $A000 in PAL, propagating
carry into the integer word. Acceleration stops once the integer part
is at least four; this test does not clamp an existing overshoot.
On a floor or ceiling, Y velocity presses into the surface and X travels
along it. The same earthquake trigger as vertical crawling saves this
handler and selects falling without skipping the current crawl step.
Expand signed 8.8 Y velocity into $14.$12, then add one pixel in its
direction to probe floor/ceiling contact. With support, calculate the
slope-adjusted X distance and move along the surface. A clear X move
is followed by vertical alignment to a non-square slope.
The support probe collided, but X travel hit an inside corner.
Reverse Y velocity and use the X sign to select a wall-facing script.
Its initial command installs the vertical movement handler.
No floor/ceiling contact: share the vertical handler's unsupported-turn
counter. On the fourth miss save this handler and fall; otherwise reverse
X and select a wall-facing script to follow the outside corner.
Finding support resets the counter before attempting X travel.
Input X is the enemy slot. Sample the supporting edge selected by the sign
of Y velocity. A slope block with BTS subtype >= 5 selects an 8.8 multiplier;
multiply the magnitude of the 8.8 X velocity and restore its sign.
Return the 16.16 move distance in $14.$12 with X restored to EnemyIndex.
Without such a slope, just expand the original velocity to 16.16.
The stored Crawler.XVelocity is not changed by this adjustment.

lines.comment: X selects this enemy's slot in the enemy arrays.
Read the population's initialisation value; it is not a script pointer yet.
Keep the starting orientation: upside right, left, down, or up (0..3).
Each orientation pointer is a word, so double the orientation number.
Y now holds the byte offset into the orientation table.
Fetch the bank-$A3 instruction list for this starting orientation.
Replace the initialisation value with the live animation-script pointer.
Select the empty spritemap until the animation supplies a frame.
Start with no visible sprite for this enemy.
A timer of one makes the script run on its next instruction update.
Schedule the orientation script's first command.
Use the local RTL as an idle handler until the script chooses movement.
Main AI can safely dispatch before the first scripted frame.
Population parameter 1 selects the crawling-speed entry.
$00FF is the sentinel for skipping the speed-table lookup.
Skip only the speed lookup; property-based sign selection still follows.
Speed entries are words; convert the selector to a byte offset.
Y indexes the selected speed word.
Load the signed 8.8 crawling speed, in pixels per frame.
Give X the chosen speed before applying direction signs.
Start Y with the same speed before applying direction signs.
Direction signs come from properties, not the initialisation value.
Isolate the two property bits that control the initial signs.
Only property value 0 takes the X-negation path.
Read the X velocity to reverse.
Complement all bits as the first step of signed negation.
Add one to finish the two's-complement negation.
Store the reversed X direction.
Initialisation is complete; this path leaves Y unchanged.
Property value 2 requests a Y reversal instead.
Values 1 and 3 leave both velocity signs unchanged.
Read the Y velocity to reverse.
Complement the Y velocity before adding one.
Complete -YVelocity without changing its 8.8 scale.
Store the reversed Y direction.
Return to the caller; this also serves as the temporary idle handler.
Read the script's next word: a bank-$A3 movement-handler address.
Install that handler for this enemy's main AI.
Advance past the handler pointer's low byte.
Advance past its high byte to the next script word.
Return the updated script pointer in Y to the instruction interpreter.
Select this enemy's state before dispatching its movement handler.
Tail-jump within bank $A3; the handler's RTL returns to the AI caller.
Read the fractional word of the separate 16.16 falling velocity.
Supply the movement helper's fractional Y distance.
Read the signed integer word of falling velocity.
Complete the helper's signed 16.16 distance at $14.$12.
Move using the current falling velocity before applying gravity.
Carry clear means unobstructed travel; continue falling.
Check whether this enemy skipped the normal speed lookup.
The $00FF sentinel has special landing-speed handling.
Ordinary speed selectors keep their existing crawling velocities.
The sentinel case resumes with +0.5 pixels per frame in 8.8.
Give X the sentinel's post-landing crawling speed.
Give Y the same positive post-landing speed.
Reset the fall state after collision.
Clear the fractional falling velocity.
Clear the integer falling velocity.
Contact ends the run of unsupported corner turns.
Recover the crawling handler saved when falling began.
Resume that handler on the next main-AI dispatch.
Finish this landing update without another movement step.
Test the integer part before adding acceleration.
Stop accelerating once the integer part is at least four.
Skip acceleration; this does not clamp an existing overshoot.
Begin acceleration with the fractional word.
Start the fractional addition without an incoming carry.
Add 0.5 px/frame per update in NTSC, or 0.625 in PAL.
Keep the new fraction; STA preserves the carry for the next ADC.
Load the integer word without disturbing that carry.
Carry any fractional overflow into the integer velocity.
Save the complete accelerated falling velocity.
Test both words for an exactly zero fall velocity.
A nonzero fraction keeps the falling handler active.
The fraction was zero; check the integer word too.
A nonzero integer likewise keeps falling active.
Zero velocity selects the vertical-crawling handler.
Install it for the next dispatch, not a second move this update.
Return from this falling-AI update.
Check for the specific earthquake update that makes crawlers let go.
The falling transition triggers when the quake timer is $001E.
Other timer values proceed with ordinary wall crawling.
Check the earthquake type as well as its timer.
Only quake type $0014 triggers this detachment path.
Other earthquake types do not detach this crawler here.
Remember the crawling handler to resume after a landing.
Save the bank-local return-to-crawling handler.
Select the separate falling state.
Schedule falling, but continue this invocation's crawl step.
Clear the fractional distance word at $12/$13.
Start the integer word at $14/$15 with a zero sign extension.
X velocity presses into the wall while Y travels along it.
A nonnegative speed needs no negative sign extension.
Negative speed needs an all-ones integer sign extension.
Write 8.8 speed across $13/$14 to form 16.16 distance at $14.$12.
Adjust the integer part for an extra pixel toward the wall.
Nonnegative X presses one pixel farther to the right.
Negative X presses one pixel farther to the left.
The negative support-probe distance is ready.
Add one pixel in the positive X direction.
Keep the extra probe pixel in the integer distance word.
Probe wall contact with X velocity plus the extra pixel.
Carry clear means no wall was found: try an outside corner.
Wall contact breaks the streak of unsupported corner turns.
Reset the shared turn counter before travelling along the wall.
Align Y to any applicable non-square slope before Y travel.
Begin a fresh fractional word for travel along the wall.
Begin with a zero integer sign extension.
Use the stored Y speed for the actual along-wall movement.
Nonnegative Y does not need an all-ones sign extension.
Sign-extend an upward, negative Y speed.
Expand signed 8.8 Y speed into the helper's 16.16 distance.
Move along the wall using the signed Y distance.
A collision along Y is an inside corner, unlike the wall probe.
No inside corner: this wall-crawling update is complete.
Reverse the wall-normal X direction for the new surface.
Complement X as the first half of signed negation.
Add one to complete the X-velocity reversal.
Keep the reversed X speed for the next orientation.
Parameter 2 is already a byte offset into the species script tables.
The Y sign chooses the new floor/ceiling orientation.
Nonnegative Y uses the upside-up instruction list.
Negative Y selects this species' upside-down list.
Join the common script-restart path.
Select this species' upside-up list.
Install the new orientation script; it will choose horizontal crawling.
Restart the new script on its next instruction update.
Make its handler-setting command run before the new animation frame.
Finish the inside-corner transition.
Count another turn without supporting-wall contact.
Advance the unsupported-turn streak, not a general animation timer.
Keep the count across orientation changes.
Four consecutive unsupported turns are enough to stop cornering.
Earlier misses still attempt an outside-corner turn.
Save the current handler before entering the falling state.
Remember which crawling handler a landing should restore.
Select falling instead of another unsupported turn.
The next main-AI dispatch will use the falling handler.
Do not also change orientation on this falling transition.
Reverse along-wall Y motion to wrap around the outside corner.
Complement Y before adding one.
Complete the signed Y-velocity negation.
Keep the reversed Y direction for the new surface.
Index this species' orientation scripts with parameter 2.
Choose the new orientation using the reversed Y sign.
Nonnegative Y selects the upside-up list.
Negative Y selects the upside-down list.
Rejoin the shared script-restart path.
Fetch the upside-up list for this species.
Install the floor/ceiling orientation after the outside turn.
Restart the orientation script without waiting for the old timer.
Let the script install its horizontal-crawling handler.
Finish this outside-corner update.
Check the earthquake timer before the floor/ceiling crawl step.
Detachment is triggered on quake timer $001E.
Other timer values keep ordinary crawling.
The timer match alone is not sufficient to detach.
This transition is specific to earthquake type $0014.
Ignore other earthquake types here.
Read the crawling handler to resume after falling.
Save that bank-local handler for the landing path.
Choose the separate falling state.
Schedule falling without skipping the remainder of this crawl update.
Clear the fractional word for the floor/ceiling support probe.
Start the integer sign extension at zero.
Y velocity presses toward the supporting floor or ceiling.
Downward, nonnegative speed needs no negative sign extension.
Sign-extend an upward, negative Y speed.
Expand the 8.8 Y speed into 16.16 distance at $14.$12.
Add an extra support-probe pixel to the integer part.
Nonnegative Y probes one pixel farther downward.
Negative Y probes one pixel farther upward.
Use the completed negative probe distance.
Add one pixel in the downward direction.
Store the extra probe pixel without changing the fraction.
Test support with Y velocity plus the extra pixel.
No collision means the floor/ceiling support has ended.
Found support ends the unsupported-turn streak.
Reset the shared counter before attempting X travel.
Compute the slope-adjusted X distance in $14.$12; keep stored X speed.
Travel along the surface with that signed X distance.
A collision along X is an inside corner.
Keep Y aligned to a non-square slope after unobstructed X travel.
Finish the normal floor/ceiling crawl step.
Reverse the support-normal Y direction to attach to the wall.
Complement Y before completing signed negation.
Add one to finish the Y-velocity reversal.
Keep the reversed Y speed for the new wall orientation.
Parameter 2 is the species pointer-table byte offset.
The X sign selects which wall-facing script to use.
Nonnegative X selects the upside-left list.
Negative X selects this species' upside-right list.
Join the common orientation-script restart.
Fetch the upside-left list for this species.
Install the wall-facing script; it will select vertical crawling.
Run the new orientation script on its next instruction update.
Restart at the handler-setting command, not the old animation frame.
Finish the inside-corner transition.
Count another turn without floor/ceiling support.
Advance the consecutive unsupported-turn count.
Preserve this streak while cornering changes orientation.
The fourth consecutive miss switches from cornering to falling.
Earlier misses still try to follow the outside corner.
Read the current handler before replacing it with falling.
Save the crawling handler that a landing should restore.
Select falling instead of another corner turn.
Use falling on the next main-AI dispatch.
Do not also restart an orientation script on this transition.
Reverse along-surface X motion to wrap around the outside corner.
Complement X as the first step of signed negation.
Add one to complete -XVelocity.
Store the reversed X direction.
Select this species' row in the orientation pointer tables.
Choose the wall orientation from the reversed X sign.
Nonnegative X uses the upside-left list.
Negative X uses the upside-right list.
Rejoin the common instruction-list restart.
Fetch this species' upside-left list.
Install the wall-facing script after the outside turn.
Replace the old instruction timer with an immediate restart.
Let the new script install its vertical-crawling handler.
Finish this outside-corner update.
Use the enemy's X position for the supporting-block sample.
Pass the sample's X coordinate on the stack.
Start with the centre Y coordinate.
Test the Y-velocity sign without replacing the position in A.
Nonnegative Y samples the lower edge, despite this local label's name.
Subtract the hitbox radius without an incoming borrow.
Negative Y presses upward, so sample the top hitbox edge.
The upper-edge sample is ready.
Add the radius without an incoming carry.
Nonnegative Y presses downward, so sample the lower edge.
Use the last pixel inside the hitbox, not the next block below it.
Pass the sampled Y coordinate alongside the earlier X coordinate.
Resolve the block containing the stack-supplied sample point.
Get that block's index in the room's block arrays.
LevelData entries are words, so double the block index.
X now indexes the sampled block, temporarily not the enemy.
Read the sampled block's level-data word.
Keep only the block-type nibble.
Block type $1 is a slope.
Other block types use the unadjusted X velocity.
BTS entries are bytes, so return to the undoubled block index.
Read the sampled slope's BTS byte.
Keep the slope shape, discarding the other BTS bits.
Shapes below five do not use this non-square-slope adjustment.
Fall back to the ordinary speed conversion for those shapes.
Begin converting the shape number to a modifier-pair byte offset.
Each shape has a four-byte modifier pair.
Index the modifier table rather than the enemy arrays.
Load this shape's 8.8 X-speed multiplier.
Restore the enemy slot before reading its velocity.
Read the stored signed 8.8 X speed without modifying it.
Nonnegative X can go directly to unsigned multiplication.
Negative X must first be converted to its unsigned magnitude.
Finish negating X to obtain that magnitude.
Multiply two 8.8 magnitudes; the 32-bit product is a 16.16 distance.
Begin restoring a negative sign with the product's low word.
Complement the fractional word of the 32-bit product.
Start the two-word negation with a clean carry.
Add one to the complemented low word; keep its carry.
Return the negative distance's fractional word at $12.
Read the high word without disturbing the low-word carry.
Complement the high word as the other half of 32-bit negation.
Propagate the low-word carry to finish negating the whole product.
Return the signed integer distance word at $14.
Return the temporary move distance; the stored X velocity is unchanged.
Multiply speed by the slope multiplier to get a 16.16 distance.
Read the fractional word of the positive product.
Supply the movement helper's fractional X distance.
Read the integer word of the product.
Supply the movement helper's integer X distance.
Return the scaled distance without changing Crawler.XVelocity.
Restore the enemy slot after sampling the block arrays.
Clear the fractional word for an unscaled 8.8-to-16.16 conversion.
Start the integer sign extension at zero.
Use the original crawling speed when no multiplier applies.
A nonnegative speed needs no negative sign extension.
Negative X requires an all-ones sign extension.
Place 8.8 speed across $13/$14 to form signed 16.16 at $14.$12.
Return the unscaled distance; the persistent X velocity is untouched.
